title: New Jersey security deposit cap
requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit greater than one and one-half times one month's rent, and any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current deposit.
key_value: 1.5 times one month's rent; yearly increase max 10%
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in New Jersey in which the landlord collects a security deposit; prepaid funds held to secure future rent, including the last month's rent, count toward the cap.
exemptions: A pet security deposit may not be charged if, combined with the regular deposit, it exceeds one and one-half times one month's rent.
quoted_span: The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less. Any additional yearly security deposit increase may not exceed 10% of the current security deposit.

title: Security deposit held in trust; interest belongs to tenant
requirement: The deposit remains the tenant's property and must be held in trust in an interest-bearing New Jersey account; the interest or earnings belong to the tenant and must be paid in cash or credited to rent.
key_value: interest earned belongs to the tenant
coverage_conditions: Landlords holding security deposit money for residential tenancies; landlords of 10 or more units may instead invest in an insured New Jersey money market fund.
exemptions: Seasonal use or rental, meaning a term of not more than 125 consecutive days by a person with a permanent residence elsewhere.
penalty: If the landlord fails to give the annual notice or pay annual interest, the tenant may apply the deposit plus interest at 7% per annum to rent.
quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid to the tenant in cash or credited toward rent due and owing on the ren ewal or anniversary of the tenant’s lease

title: Security deposit return deadline and double-damages remedy
requirement: Within 30 days after a tenancy ends the landlord must return the deposit plus interest less deductions, with an itemized list of deductions; the deadline is 5 business days after displacement by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation.
coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies in which the landlord holds a security deposit.
exemptions: No deduction may be made from the security deposit of a tenant who remains in possession of the rental premises.
penalty: The tenant may sue for double the amount wrongfully withheld, together with court costs and reasonable attorney's fees.
quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

title: Security deposit return after Safe Housing Act lease termination
requirement: When a tenant ends a lease early under the Safe Housing Act, the landlord must make the security deposit plus interest available for return within 15 business days and tell the tenant within 3 business days where to collect it.
coverage_conditions: Tenants who terminate a lease before its expiration under the New Jersey Safe Housing Act because of domestic violence.
exemptions: Does not apply to transient or seasonal rentals.
quoted_span: If a tenant terminates the lease agreement prior to the expiration of the lease pursuant to the Safe Housing Act , (N.J.S.A. 46:8-9.6), the tenant is entitled to the return of their security deposit. Within 15 business days after the lease  is terminated, the landlord shall make available the return of the tenant’s security deposit, plus any interest earned, to the tenant or the tenant’s agent.

title: New owner's duty on transfer of the property
requirement: When rental property is sold or transferred, the new owner must obtain the tenant's security deposit plus accrued interest and is responsible for investing it, giving notices, paying interest, and returning it.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies whose security deposit was collected by a former owner when the property is sold or transferred.
quoted_span: If the property is sold or transferred it is the duty of the new owner to obtain the security deposit, plus accrued interest on the tenant’s deposit, that was collected by the former owner.

title: Penalty for withholding a subsidized tenant's deposit
requirement: A landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds the security deposit of a tenant who received State or federal financial assistance, including welfare or rental assistance, is liable for a civil penalty for each offense.
coverage_conditions: Security deposits made by or on behalf of tenants who received financial assistance through any State or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance.
penalty: Civil penalty of not less than $500 and not more than $2,000 per offense, collected by summary proceedings; the State entity that made the deposit is entitled to the penalty recovered.
quoted_span: Any landlord who willfully and intentionally withholds a security deposit made by or on behalf of a tenant who has received financial assistance through any Stat e or federal program, including welfare or rental assistance , may be penalized. The landlord may be liable for a civil penalty of not less than $500 or not more than $2,000 for each offense.

title: Unlawful use of security deposit money
requirement: No person may unlawfully use security deposit money; a violation is a disorderly persons offense punishable by fine, imprisonment, or both.
key_value: fine of at least $200, up to 30 days imprisonment
coverage_conditions: Any person who receives or holds security deposit money for a residential tenancy.
penalty: Charged as a disorderly person: fine of not less than $200 or imprisonment for not more than 30 days, or both.
quoted_span: Any person who unlawfully uses security deposit monies may be c riminally charged as a disorderly person and may be subject to a fine of not less than $200 or imprisonment for not more than 30 days, or both (N.J.S.A. 46:8-25).

title: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control
requirement: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from any municipal rent control or rent leveling ordinance for 30 years after completion of construction of the building.
coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings; rents subsidized by governmental funding may also be exempt from local rent control ordinances.
exemptions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings, and rents subsidized by governmental funding, are exempt from municipal rent control ordinances.
quoted_span: Under the Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law ( N.J.S.A. 2A:42 -84.5), newly constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period of 30 years following completion of construction of the building.

title: Unconscionable rent increase barred under the Anti-Eviction Act
requirement: Before evicting for nonpayment of a rent increase the landlord must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase, and the increase must not be unconscionable or violate a municipal rent ordinance.
key_value: rent increase must not be unconscionable
coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act; a landlord may raise rent only by terminating the old lease and offering a new lease at the increased rent.
penalty: The tenant may file a complaint with a municipal rent control board where one exists; otherwise a judge decides whether the increase is unconscionable in the eviction action.
quoted_span: The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
interaction: The increase must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases where such ordinances exist.

title: No rent increase to cover condominium or cooperative conversion costs
requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership of units, the landlord may not raise rents to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion.
coverage_conditions: All tenants in a converted building, whether or not they are eligible for protected tenancy as senior citizens or disabled persons.
exemptions: Rents may still be increased to cover the cost of new services or amenities.
quoted_span: If a building is converted to a condominium or cooperative form of ownership, or to fee simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the conversion (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.31).

title: Anti-Eviction Act good cause requirement
requirement: No residential landlord may evict a tenant or fail to renew a lease, written or oral, without good cause, and the landlord must be able to prove the grounds for eviction in court.
coverage_conditions: Residential tenants protected by the Anti-Eviction Act, N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 to 61.12; a landlord may recover possession only by tenant consent or the legal eviction process.
quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause. The landlord must be able to prove in court that he has grounds for an eviction.

title: Notice to Quit required for good cause evictions
requirement: For every good cause eviction except nonpayment of rent, the landlord must describe the cause in detail in a written notice to the tenant and serve a Notice to Quit; a Notice to Cease may also be required.
coverage_conditions: All good cause evictions of residential tenants; the notice requirement does not apply to evictions for nonpayment of rent.
exemptions: No Notice to Quit is required for an eviction for nonpayment of rent.
quoted_span: Each cause, except for nonpayment of rent, must be described in detail by the landlord in a written notice to the tenant. A “Notice to Quit” is required for all good cause evictions, except for an eviction for nonpayment of rent ( N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.2).

title: Law Against Discrimination source-of-income protection
requirement: A landlord must treat applicants and tenants equally in the rental of housing and may not discriminate on the basis of source of lawful income, along with the other protected characteristics listed in the Law Against Discrimination.
coverage_conditions: All landlord-tenant relationships in New Jersey, with exceptions for two-family owner-occupied dwellings and rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home.
exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings; rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home; residences planned exclusively for and occupied by one sex, as it pertains to familial status.
penalty: Landlords who violate the Law Against Discrimination are subject to fines and penalties up to $10,000 for a first offense.
quoted_span: prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, nationality, or source of lawful income.

title: Tenant-paid credit report cost and application fees
requirement: A landlord may charge an applicant the cost of a credit report and may also request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification; no dollar cap is stated in the guide.
key_value: cost of the credit report; reasonable application fees
coverage_conditions: Prospective residential tenants screened through credit bureaus or tenant screening agencies in New Jersey.
citation: Truth in Renting: Credit Checks and Background Checks
quoted_span: The landlord is allowed to charge the tenant for the cost of the report. The landlord may also request reasonable rental application fees or employment verification.
